questions.question: What is the status of the event which bought "Post Cards, Posters" on 2019/8/20?
questions.evidence: 'Post Cards, Posters' is an expense description; on 2019/8/20 refers to expense_date = '2019-8-20'; status of event refers to event_status
questions.SQL: SELECT T1.event_status FROM budget AS T1 INNER JOIN expense AS T2 ON T1.budget_id = T2.link_to_budget WHERE T2.expense_description = 'Post Cards, Posters' AND T2.expense_date = '2019-08-20'

questions.question: Which department was the President of the club in?
questions.evidence: 'President' is a position of Student Club
questions.SQL: SELECT T2.department FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id WHERE T1.position = 'President'

questions.question: For all the club members from "Business" major, how many of them wear medium size t-shirt?
questions.evidence: 'Business' is a major name; wear medium size t-shirt refers to t_shirt_size = 'Medium'
questions.SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.member_id) FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id WHERE T2.major_name = 'Business' AND T1.t_shirt_size = 'Medium'

questions.question: Calculate the total average cost that Elijah Allen spent in the events on September and October.
questions.evidence: Elijah Allen is the full name; full name refers to first_name, last_name; The 5th and 6th string of the expense_date in the expense table can refer to month; events in September and October refers to month(expense_date) = 9 OR month(expense_date) = 10
questions.SQL: SELECT AVG(T2.cost) FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN expense AS T2 ON T1.member_id = T2.link_to_member WHERE T1.last_name = 'Allen' AND T1.first_name = 'Elijah' AND (SUBSTR(T2.expense_date, 6, 2) = '09' OR SUBSTR(T2.expense_date, 6, 2) = '10')

questions.question: Which event has the lowest cost?
questions.evidence: event refers to event_name; lowest cost means MIN(cost)
questions.SQL: SELECT T1.event_name FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget ORDER BY T3.cost LIMIT 1

questions.question: List the full name of the Student_Club members that grew up in Illinois state.
questions.evidence: full name of member refers to first_name, last_name
questions.SQL: SELECT T1.first_name, T1.last_name FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN zip_code AS T2 ON T1.zip = T2.zip_code WHERE T2.state = 'Illinois'

questions.question: State what kind of expenses that Sacha Harrison incurred?
questions.evidence: kind of expenses refers to expense_description; Sacha Harrison is the full name; full name refers to first_name, last_name;
questions.SQL: SELECT T2.expense_description FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN expense AS T2 ON T1.member_id = T2.link_to_member WHERE T1.first_name = 'Sacha' AND T1.last_name = 'Harrison'

questions.question: How many times was the budget in Advertisement for "Yearly Kickoff" meeting more than "October Meeting"?
questions.evidence: budget in Advertisement refer to category = 'Advertisement' in the budget table; DIVIDE(SUM(amount when event_name = 'Yearly Kickoff'), SUM(amount when event_name = 'October Meeting'))
questions.SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.event_name = 'Yearly Kickoff' THEN T1.amount ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN T2.event_name = 'October Meeting' THEN T1.amount ELSE 0 END) FROM budget AS T1 INNER JOIN event AS T2 ON T1.link_to_event = T2.event_id WHERE T1.category = 'Advertisement' AND T2.type = 'Meeting'

questions.question: Identify the type of expenses and their total value approved for 'October Meeting' event.
questions.evidence: total value refers to SUM(cost); 'October Meeting' is an event name;
questions.SQL: SELECT T1.type, SUM(T3.cost) FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget WHERE T1.event_name = 'October Meeting'

questions.question: How many members attended the "Women's Soccer" event?
questions.evidence: 'Women's Soccer' is the event name;
questions.SQL: SELECT COUNT(T2.link_to_member) FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN attendance AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event WHERE T1.event_name = 'Women''s Soccer'

questions.question: What is the highest amount of budget spend for an event?
questions.evidence: highest amount of budget spend refers to MAX(spent)
questions.SQL: SELECT MAX(spent) FROM budget

questions.question: Give the full name and contact number of members who had to spend more than average on each expense.
questions.evidence: full name refers to first_name, last_name; contact number refers to phone; had spent more than average on each expense refers to cost > AVG(cost)
questions.SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T3.first_name, T3.last_name, T3.phone FROM expense AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.link_to_budget = T2.budget_id INNER JOIN member AS T3 ON T3.member_id = T1.link_to_member WHERE T1.cost > ( SELECT AVG(T1.cost) FROM expense AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.link_to_budget = T2.budget_id INNER JOIN member AS T3 ON T3.member_id = T1.link_to_member )

questions.question: Among all the closed events, which event has the highest spend-to-budget ratio?
questions.evidence: closed events refers to event_name where status = 'Closed'; highest spend-to budget ratio refers to MAX(DIVIDE(spent, amount))
questions.SQL: SELECT T2.event_name FROM budget AS T1 INNER JOIN event AS T2 ON T1.link_to_event = T2.event_id WHERE T2.status = 'Closed' ORDER BY T1.spent / T1.amount DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: Indicate the name of the closed event whose cost has exceeded the budget the most.
questions.evidence: closed events refers to event_name where status = 'Closed'; exceed the budget the most refers to MIN(remaining) where remaining < 0
questions.SQL: SELECT T2.event_name FROM budget AS T1 INNER JOIN event AS T2 ON T2.event_id = T1.link_to_event WHERE T1.event_status = 'Closed' AND T1.remaining < 0 ORDER BY T1.remaining LIMIT 1

questions.question: What does the person with the phone number "809-555-3360" major in?
questions.evidence: major in refers to major_name
questions.SQL: SELECT T2.major_name FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id WHERE T1.phone = '809-555-3360'

questions.question: How many cities are there in Orange County, Virginia?
questions.evidence: Orange County is the county name, Virginia is the state name
questions.SQL: SELECT COUNT(city) FROM zip_code WHERE county = 'Orange County' AND state = 'Virginia'

questions.question: List all the names of events that had an attendance of over 20 students but were not fundraisers.
questions.evidence: name of events refers to event_name; attendance of over 20 students COUNT(event_id) > 20.
questions.SQL: SELECT T1.event_name FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN attendance AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event GROUP BY T1.event_id HAVING COUNT(T2.link_to_event) > 20 EXCEPT SELECT T1.event_name FROM event AS T1  WHERE T1.type = 'Fundraiser'

questions.question: What is the total cost of the pizzas for all the events?
questions.evidence: total cost of the pizzas refers to SUM(cost) where expense_description = 'Pizza'
questions.SQL: SELECT SUM(cost) FROM expense WHERE expense_description = 'Pizza'

questions.question: List out the full name and total cost that member id "rec4BLdZHS2Blfp4v" incurred?
questions.evidence: full name refers to first_name, last name
questions.SQL: SELECT T1.first_name, T1.last_name, SUM(T2.cost) FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN expense AS T2 ON T1.member_id = T2.link_to_member WHERE T1.member_id = 'rec4BLdZHS2Blfp4v'

questions.question: Indicate the top source of funds received in September 2019 based on their amount.
questions.evidence: top source funds refers to MAX(source); September 2019 means date_received BETWEEN '2019-09-01' and '2019-09-30'
questions.SQL: SELECT source FROM income WHERE date_received BETWEEN '2019-09-01' and '2019-09-30' ORDER BY source DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: Which student has been entrusted to manage the budget for the Yearly Kickoff?
questions.evidence: name of students means the full name; full name refers to first_name, last_name;'Yearly Kickoff' is an event name;
questions.SQL: SELECT T4.first_name, T4.last_name FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget INNER JOIN member AS T4 ON T3.link_to_member = T4.member_id WHERE T1.event_name = 'Yearly Kickoff'

questions.question: Among the students from the Student_Club who attended the event "Women's Soccer", how many of them want a T-shirt that's in medium size?
questions.evidence: Women's Soccer is an event name; T-shirt that is in medium size refers to t_shirt_size = 'Medium'
questions.SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.event_id) FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN attendance AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN member AS T3 ON T2.link_to_member = T3.member_id WHERE T1.event_name = 'Women''s Soccer' AND T3.t_shirt_size = 'Medium'

questions.question: Was each expense in October Meeting on October 8, 2019 approved?
questions.evidence: event_name = 'October Meeting' where event_date = '2019-10-08'; approved = True means expenses was approved; approved = False means expenses was not approved
questions.SQL: SELECT T3.approved FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget WHERE T1.event_name = 'October Meeting' AND T1.event_date LIKE '2019-10-08%'

questions.question: How many members of the Student_Club have major in 'Physics Teaching'?
questions.evidence: 'Physics Teaching' is the major_name;
questions.SQL: SELECT COUNT(T2.member_id) FROM major AS T1 INNER JOIN member AS T2 ON T1.major_id = T2.link_to_major WHERE T1.major_name = 'Physics Teaching'
